steps.title: The question
steps.say: Seasons are not caused by Earth being closer to or farther from the Sun. They come from something else: Earth's tilt.

steps.title: Sun and Earth
steps.say: Picture the Sun on the left, shining light toward Earth on the right.

steps.title: The tilted axis
steps.say: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5 degrees, and it always points toward the same direction in space.

steps.title: Summer in the north
steps.say: When the north end leans toward the Sun, sunlight hits the north more directly and days are longer. That is summer there.

ops.text:
North leans toward Sun:
direct light, long days
= NORTH SUMMER

steps.title: Winter in the north
steps.say: Half a year later Earth is on the other side, and the north leans away. Light is slanted and spread thin, so it is winter.

ops.text:
North leans away:
slanted light, short days
= NORTH WINTER

steps.title: Summary
steps.say: So the tilt, not the distance, changes how strongly sunlight hits each hemisphere, and that gives us the seasons.

ops.text: Tilt → light angle + day length → seasons
